duration_excerpt:
Duration
The consultation will run for 13 weeks starting on 22 June 2026 and ending on 21 September 2026.
scope_excerpt:
3. Scope
In scope
The government is proposing that mandatory registration requirements should:
apply UK wide for intermediaries who interact with
HMRC
apply to both imports and exports
apply consistently across all customs activity, rather than being limited to specific declaration types
Out of scope
The government is proposing that mandatory registration should not apply to:
intermediaries who provide advice only and do not interact with
HMRC
on behalf of traders
hauliers and carriers as their interaction with
HMRC
is to fulfil their own legal obligations and does not involve making or amending customs declarations on behalf of traders
self-representation to ensure the proposed policy targets customs intermediary related harm without creating unnecessary burdens for traders
next_steps_excerpt:
6. Next steps
Following this consultation, the government intends to:
consider responses carefully and publish a summary of feedback
refine the policy design where appropriate
confirm next steps on legislation and implementation
partial_response_excerpt: Not all questions in this consultation will be relevant to everyone, and respondents may choose to answer some or all of the questions. HMRC welcomes partial responses, focussed on aspects of customs that are most relevant to the respondent.

questions.text: What is the name of your business/organisation?
What type of business are you? (such as clothes retailer, car manufacturer, freight forwarder, fast parcel operator, haulier)
If applicable, how many movements do you make per year? Are they imports, exports, or both?

If you selected ‘customs intermediary’, what type of intermediary are you? (Select all that apply)
customs agent or broker
express operator
freight forwarder
warehouse operator
haulier
other (please specify)

What is the size of your business?
micro (1 to 9 employees)
small (10 to 49 employees)
medium (50 to 249 employees)
large (over 250 employees)
If applicable, how long has your business been importing or exporting goods, or supporting traders to import/export if you are an intermediary?

What do you think the benefits and/or challenges are of the government introducing mandatory registration requirements that customs intermediaries must satisfy to submit customs declarations on behalf of traders?
What are your views on the proposed scope of the mandatory requirements?
Do you consider the proposed minimum requirements appropriate and proportionate, and are there specific requirements that should be added, removed or amended?
What are your views on the proposed enforcement approach, including the use of a graduated and proportionate model?

The government intends to provide a transitional period to support implementation of the proposed requirements. What length of transitional period do you consider appropriate, and are there any specific factors that should be taken into account in determining its duration?
Do you foresee any broad unintended consequences, or impacts on trade arising from the implementation of these proposals?

Are there any other design considerations the government should take into account when developing mandatory registration requirements, including any additional steps it could take to support high-quality intermediaries and prevent non-compliant or harmful intermediaries from operating?
